transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-12 16:00 PT | Duration: 38 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen, Dev Patel (Redwood); Lena Ortiz, Mark Rivers, Sophie Chan (Aurora)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE for Redwood, and Dev (pointing) will run the demo. How's everybody doing?
[00:06] Lena: Doing good, thanks. Excited to see the eval stuff — we've been, uh, pretty hit-or-miss with post-deploy regressions lately.
[00:12] Dev: Great. Quick agenda — show prompt-set workflow in Console, regression alerting, and A/B compare dashboards, and then how you can wire this into your CI/CD and API. We'll keep it practical.
[00:20] Mark: High-level: our main goal is to avoid silent regressions after model swaps and to have a way to compare variants for cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:27] Dev: Perfect, that's exactly what we'll cover.
[01:02] [screen share starts] Dev: Ok, so inside Redwood Console — apologies if the shared view lags, sometimes the screen share is a hair behind — here's the Eval tab. You can upload prompt sets, tag them (prod, onboarding, fraud-check), and attach expected outputs or evaluation heuristics.
[01:25] Dev: For Aurora, you'd likely want to split by customer-facing and internal prompts. You can see we support both structured oracle answers and fuzzy metrics like F1/ROUGE or custom LLM heuristics.
[01:40] Sophie: Quick Q — can we do golden references plus human labels? Some of our prompts need human ground truth.
[01:46] Dev: Yes, you can attach human-labeled examples; the system will surface disagreement rates and annotator drift. We also keep provenance for each example. (note: sometimes 'provenance' came out as 'pro vino nce' in the transcript)
[02:15] [00:02:15] Lena: How often do you run evals — is it continuous or scheduled?
[02:22] Dev: Both. You can run on a schedule (daily/nightly) or trigger via API on deploy. We recommend a quick smoke eval on deploy and a more thorough nightly run.
[03:05] Dev: Here's prompt-set versioning — every change produces a diff and we keep historical metrics. If a new model causes a drop in, say, 'helpfulness' by more than your threshold, an alert is created.
[03:35] [00:03:35] Mark: Thresholds — are those customizable? Our product team is pretty conservative so we'd set tight thresholds.
[03:42] Dev: Totally. You can set per-metric, per-prompt-set thresholds, and choose severity (info/warn/critical). Alerts can post to Slack, email, or create a ticket in Jira via webhook.
[04:10] [crosstalk] Sophie: And what about A/B? We run multiple model families and want side-by-side comparisons.
[04:17] Dev: A/B dashboard shows aligned examples, per-example diffs, and metrics across variants. You can define win conditions (lower hallucination, better token-economy). It also computes statistical significance for sample sizes.
[04:40] Lena: Sample size — what's the recommended minimum? We have a mix of high-signal and noisy prompts.
[04:47] Dev: Depends on metric variance; for discrete labels 200-500 examples per variant is a baseline; for fuzzy metrics you might want 1k+. For Aurora, starting with 1k prompt seed makes sense.
[05:15] [00:05:15] Maya: A quick note on cost: Redwood's Optimize will suggest quantized model variants and batching settings to hit cost targets while keeping quality. We can show how that ties into the A/B comparisons.
[05:30] Mark: If we pick a quantized variant to save cost, will the eval detect quality regressions introduced by quantization?
[05:37] Dev: Yes, you can include any variant (float32, int8 q, etc.) as a model in the eval suite. The system computes per-metric deltas and alerts on regressions.
[06:05] [00:06:05] Sophie: Integration — do we need to export examples or can we stream logs from our infra?
[06:11] Dev: Both. You can POST examples via API, or we can connect to your logging pipeline; we also support S3/CSV imports for bulk uploads.
[06:35] [00:06:35] Lena: Security concerns — we need VPC, SOC 2, and KMS for any customer PII.
[06:42] Maya: For Private deployments we offer VPC connectors and you can bring your KMS/HSM. For hosted, we have SOC 2 and can integrate with your SSO. Dev will share the security pack.
[07:05] Dev: I just uploaded the security doc link in the chat — also note audit logs for eval runs are retained per your retention policy.
[07:20] [00:07:20] Mark: How heavy is the eval compute? If we run nightly on large prompt sets it could spike costs.
[07:27] Dev: We have sampling strategies and incremental evals — only newly seen prompts or those where the model output changed are re-evaluated, and you can set a cost cap. Also Optimize suggests batching and reuse of KV cache to reduce per-token cost.
[08:10] [00:08:10] Sophie: Example outputs — can the dashboard surface tokens where hallucination occurs?
[08:16] Dev: Yes, per-example highlights and a culprit-token view; it will flag hallucinated entities using heuristics and optional NER ground truth.
[08:45] [00:08:45] Maya: Let's demo a regression alert — Dev, can you flip to the 'alerts' view?
[08:50] Dev: Sure. Here's an alert triggered last week when a model update dropped 'accuracy' on the payments prompt set by 7%. You can see the delta, the per-example list, and a sample of top failing prompts.
[09:20] Dev: From here you can triage: mark as accepted, assign to owner, or kick off a rollback via the deployment integration.
[09:40] Lena: Rollback — does Redwood integrate with our deploy pipeline (we use GitHub Actions + Terraform)?
[09:47] Dev: Yup, webhook based. If you want automatic rollback on critical regressions that's possible but we usually recommend a manual gate for safety.
[10:15] [00:10:15] Mark: We also run A/B online tests in prod. Can Redwood ingest online metrics to combine with offline evals?
[10:22] Dev: Yes, you can import online metrics (click-through, conversion) and correlate them with eval scores to get a unified view.
[11:00] [00:11:00] Sophie: About the API — how fast is the feedback loop? If we POST 1k examples to the eval API, how quickly do we get results?
[11:07] Dev: Depends on model latency and eval complexity. For simple metrics we can stream results back within minutes; heavy large-metric computations may be queued and available in an hour. We expose a progress endpoint.
[12:00] [00:12:00] (minor audio blip)
[12:25] Dev: Now switching to A/B compare: see side-by-side examples, sortable by delta in hallucination and latency. You can also group by prompt category.
[12:50] Sophie: Can we save a comparison as a report to share with product?
[12:55] Dev: Yes, exportable PDF and CSV. You can also schedule recurring reports.
[13:30] [00:13:30] Lena: Any built-in tests for bias or safety for retail domain? We sometimes get offensive or problematic output in certain prompts.
[13:38] Dev: We have a safety heuristics library and custom checks you can add — e.g., profanity filters, policy classifiers, or domain-specific rules. You can also run the eval against red-team prompt sets.
[14:05] Maya: Quick note on data retention: for pilot, we'll keep eval data 90 days unless Aurora needs longer, which we can arrange under Private agreements.
[14:30] [00:14:30] Mark: Ok, technical deep-dive — what's the eval architecture? Do you compute diffs client-side or in Redwood infra?
[14:38] Dev: All eval computations run in Redwood's eval cluster; we support on-prem/private eval compute for sensitive datasets. The engine reuses KV cache when comparing variants to keep latency consistent. (sometimes transcribed as 'KV cash')
[15:10] Lena: Do you support custom metrics? For example, we have a 'brand voice adherence' score trained internally.
[15:16] Dev: You can plug in custom metric functions via a simple lambda interface or upload metric results. We'll surface them in the same dashboard.
[16:00] [00:16:00] Sophie: For A/B significance, does Redwood compute p-values or bootstrap CIs?
[16:06] Dev: We do both — p-values for categorical metrics and bootstrap confidence intervals for continuous/fuzzy metrics. The dashboard also shows required N for desired power.
[17:00] [00:17:00] (slight overlap/crosstalk)
[17:20] Maya: We're getting to time — quick Q on onboarding: what's typical timeline for a pilot?
[17:27] Dev: For a 1-week pilot: day 0 onboarding and SSO + VPC check, day 1-2 upload prompt sets and baseline eval, day 3 run A/B and regressions, day 4 iterate prompts, day 5 deliver report. If Aurora needs private infra that's longer (2-3 weeks).
[18:05] Lena: One blocker: data residency — some of our EU customers' prompts must stay in EU. Can we pin eval compute to region?
[18:12] Dev: Yes, region pinning is supported for Private and dedicated pools; for hosted we have EU regions with residency options.
[18:40] [00:18:40] Mark: Pricing question — do you charge per-eval-run or by tokens used for eval?
[18:47] Maya: We charge by compute/eval unit with token proxies; for pilots we can do a capped price. We'll include details in the SOW.
[19:10] Dev: Also Optimize will estimate cost per thousand eval examples for each model variant so you can see unit economics upfront.
[20:00] [00:20:00] (background noise)
[20:25] Sophie: A practical ask — can you surface failing examples with context (user history) while preserving PII? We need redaction.
[20:32] Dev: Redwood supports field-level redaction during ingest and a pseudonymization flow; you can also run transformations client-side before upload.
[21:05] [00:21:05] Lena: Ok, let's talk acceptance criteria for pilot: 1) detect regressions >5% on key prompts, 2) provide A/B report comparing two variants, 3) integration with our Slack for alerts.
[21:20] Maya: Noted — sounds reasonable. We'll include those in the pilot scope.
[22:10] [00:22:10] Mark: Any references or case studies for retail we can read?
[22:17] Maya: I'll send a short retail case study where we caught several regressions after a quantized rollout.
[22:35] Dev: Also sharing a sample eval dashboard and the CSV export used.
[23:00] [00:23:00] (screen share shows export)
[23:30] Lena: How do we set up Slack alerts only for criticals? We get too many messages.
[23:37] Dev: Alert routing supports severity filters and grouping. We can set a quiet window for noisy tests.
[24:10] [00:24:10] Sophie: Any mention of competitor lock-in? We want portable prompts and artifacts.
[24:16] Maya: All prompt sets and metrics are exportable; no vendor lock-in — you can migrate artifacts via S3 export.
[24:50] Dev: Quick demo of the API call pattern for submitting prompt batches — here's a curl example (note: the transcript transcribed a token name as 'red wood token' once).
[25:20] Mark: We'll need the SDK example for Python and our infra.
[25:26] Dev: We'll send the SDK snippet in the follow-up.
[26:00] [00:26:00] (short pause)
[26:30] Lena: Anything else on compliance? We will need contract language for data handling.
[26:37] Maya: We'll include standard data processing addendum and can work with legal.
[27:10] [00:27:10] Sophie: Pilot measurement — who owns triage once an alert fires? We want clear handoff.
[27:18] Maya: We usually recommend a joint rota for the pilot — Redwood SE for triage and Aurora assigns an owner; we'll capture that in the SOW.
[28:00] [00:28:00] Dev: Quick note — you can automate regression triage rules, e.g., auto-assign to ML owner when hallucination rate crosses X.
[28:25] Lena: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[28:30] Maya: Recap: I'll send pilot SOW and pricing (due 8/14), Dev will share security pack + SDK snippets (due 8/13), Aurora will provide the 1k prompt seed (Sophie, due 8/16). We'll schedule kickoff week of 8/24.
[29:05] [00:29:05] Mark: Sounds good. Any blockers?
[29:10] Lena: None on this call.
[29:20] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links.
[29:35] [00:29:35] (call winds down)
[30:00] End call notes: length ~38 minutes (some people left early).

Transcription notes: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'KV cache' -> 'K-V cash', 'provenance' slightly garbled), filler words and crosstalk present.
